## Conclusion

I retrieved both official sources. The latest macOS arm64 **CLI** manifest matches the caller’s installed version. Public session-continuation syntax differs from the caller’s local help; compatibility remains unverified.

## Scope and research date

**2026-10-09, Asia/Seoul.** Read-only inspection of the two named public sources. No private data, settings changes, installations, or command execution.

## 1. Latest CLI version

The manifest returns <citation refs="AnE376tUOXFpSDzZIFVTf">`"version": "1.26.1008.1938"` and `"platform": "darwin-arm64"`</citation>.

Exact URL: https://releases.aside.com/cli/AsideCLI-darwin-arm64-latest.json

Its `/cli/AsideCLI-…` identity establishes that this is CLI metadata, not desktop-app metadata. It agrees with the caller-supplied installed version. The JSON contains no release date.

## 2. Session continuation: documentation drift

The official developer page <citation refs="DTTQABsoX-pPyu4_Z4V0j">says “Use `--session` to continue an existing session” and shows `aside --session <session-id> "Continue"`</citation>.

Exact URL: https://docs.aside.com/help/developers

**Caller-supplied local observation:** installed help instead documents `aside session resume`, accepting a session ID and optional prompt, with only `--account` as a command option. The caller also reports `--effort ultrabrowse` under `aside exec --help`; this is not a public-documentation finding.

**Assessment:** both describe continuation of an existing session, but their documented command forms differ. The retrieved public page does not document `aside session resume`. This establishes documentation drift, **not** that the older `--session` form fails. No release-version marker or publication/update date appears in the retrieved developer content, so it cannot be attributed specifically to the installed release.

## Claim ledger

| Claim | Original URL / title / publisher | Evidence class | Date/version | Confidence | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1: latest CLI matches installed version | https://releases.aside.com/cli/AsideCLI-darwin-arm64-latest.json · No human-readable title; manifest filename · Aside | Retrieved official metadata | Version above; release date absent | High | Mutable “latest” endpoint |
| Q2: public continuation form | https://docs.aside.com/help/developers · “Use the CLI, MCP, and REPL - Aside Help Center” · Aside | Retrieved source-owner documentation | No document date/version found | High | Compatibility not tested |
| Current installed help | No public URL; caller’s local CLI help | Caller-supplied observation | Installed version above | Supplied, not independently verified | Exact help output not rerun |
| Syntax drift | Comparison of Q2 and local observation | Inference | Research date above | High for differing forms | Runtime equivalence unknown |

## Limitations

This verifies current official evidence retrieval, not CLI execution or general workflow reliability. Documentation text was retrieved through web fetch; the browser exposed its title but no body content. The manifest was also confirmed in the browser.

## Session-continuation audit

The developer page shows <citation refs="DTTQABsoX-pPyu4_Z4V0j">`aside --session <session-id> "Continue"`</citation>.

Original URL: https://docs.aside.com/help/developers

The caller-observed installed **1.26.1008.1938** help instead shows:

`aside session resume <id> [prompt...]`

These are different command forms for the same stated purpose. The retrieved public page has **no explicit release-version marker or publication/update date**; it cannot be assigned specifically to 1.26.1008.1938.

**Still unverified:** whether the installed CLI accepts the public `--session` form as an alias, whether both forms behave equivalently, and whether either succeeds at runtime. No continuation command was executed, and local help remains caller-supplied evidence.

**Audit result:** public evidence **confirms the syntax discrepancy but narrows the original “documentation drift” conclusion**. It establishes a difference between public documentation and reported current help, not incompatibility, removal, or deprecation of the public syntax.
